spot: Wetlands boardwalk & two wildlife observation decks (base of quarry)

detail.reason: Lowest point in the park: a quarry depression below roadway grade. Directly contradicts the single dominant high-place signature.
Enclosed wetland in a pit; no broad outward vista over valleys/water.
Host features are wooden boardwalks/decks, not a natural above-ground rock crevice or undercut.
Boardwalk structures sit above ground, but any hide would be man-made wood, not a natural ledge/hollow at a rock or tree base.
Operative landmark is wooden decks and standing water, not a boulder/slab/sittable stone.
Water is THE feature, but boardwalks go over the water (crossing it), opposite of the dry-bank-beside-water intent.
Developed wetland-restoration/outdoor-classroom area, not a forest edge meeting a clearing.
Reached on a 0.3-mi paved ADA loop with easy, non-dangerous footing.
Essentially roadside, adjacent to Rocky Face Church Road; no water crossing or cliff scaling to reach.
Highly visible, signed, frequently-visited interpretive feature, not secluded or off the obvious view.
No gap/saddle/notch between paired rock features here.
No prominent oak/pine marker noted; the markers are built structures.
No eastward orientation cue for the spot or its view.
No domed/egg/round stone marker present.
Wetland vegetation, but not green moss/lichen set against dark exposed stone.
No quartz/crystalline host rock; the medium is water and wood.
No angular/faceted/stratified rock feature at this spot.
No warm-toned/reddish stone cue.
No pale/white stone marker.
It is a quarry depression/basin that traps water, a weak basin-shape echo, but earthen pit not a rock bowl.
No confluence or watercourse bend; it is a static constructed pond.
One descends below grade to reach it, but it ends low, not at a high spot, so only half the cue fits.
Interpretive 'what to look for' signage exists, but that is large posted signage, not a small overlooked seam/inscription to read up close.
No left-turn directional nudge associated with the approach.
Open-air, but sheltered low in a depression rather than a breezy ridge/overhang.
Boardwalk posts are countable but there is no specific measured-count cue tied here.
